hero.body: Private journeys, planned end to end. We shape the route, choose the stays and arrange your driver, then leave you the hours in between.

regions.name: Cultural Triangle
regions.alt: Sigiriya rock seen from Pidurangala at first light
regions.body: Sigiriya, Dambulla, Polonnaruwa and Anuradhapura sit within an hour or two of each other. A rock fortress, painted cave temples and two ancient capitals, all best seen early, before the heat and the coaches arrive.
regions.known: Sigiriya at dawn, the Dambulla caves

regions.name: Hill Country
regions.alt: The train crossing the Nine Arch Bridge near Ella
regions.body: Tea estates, waterfalls and a railway line that seems to have been built for the view. Nuwara Eliya is cool enough for a jumper, Ella is slower than you expect, and the train between them is the ride people talk about for years.
regions.months: January to April, July to September
regions.known: The Ella train, tea at first light
regions.access: 5 hours by road, or the train up from Kandy

regions.name: Kandy and the centre
regions.alt: The Temple of the Tooth lit up across Kandy lake
regions.body: The last royal capital, wrapped around a lake. The Temple of the Tooth as the lamps come on, drummers in the evening, and the botanical gardens the next morning before the road climbs into the hills.
regions.months: Year round, driest December to April
regions.known: Temple of the Tooth, Kandyan drummers

regions.name: The national parks
regions.alt: A leopard crossing the track in front of a safari jeep
regions.body: Yala for leopards, Udawalawe and Minneriya for elephants, Wilpattu for the quiet. We plan around the hours the animals are actually out, which means one early start rather than five, and a guide who knows the park rather than just the route.
regions.months: February to July, Minneriya July to September
regions.known: Leopards in Yala, the Minneriya gathering
regions.access: Yala is 5 hours from Colombo, 2 from Galle

regions.name: The south coast
regions.alt: An empty stretch of sand on the south coast
regions.body: Galle Fort in the last hour of light, whales off Mirissa between November and April, and beaches at Tangalle where the evening walk is the whole plan. This is where most journeys end, and nobody minds.
regions.access: 2 hours from Colombo on the expressway

planningSteps.title: You tell us what matters
planningSteps.body: Two short steps on the planning form, or a message if you would rather write it out. Dates, rough budget, and what you would hate to rush.

planningSteps.title: We send a first route
planningSteps.body: A suggested route with the stays we would use and a full price, usually within a few working days. No charge and no obligation at this point.

planningSteps.title: You change it until it fits
planningSteps.body: Swap a stay, add a night, drop a stop. We redraw as often as it takes, and nothing is booked while you are still deciding.

planningSteps.title: Book, then travel
planningSteps.body: A deposit confirms the booking, with the balance due before you fly. Your planner stays reachable the whole time you are here.

homeQuestions.q: How much time should we allow for Sri Lanka?
homeQuestions.a: Ten nights is the sweet spot for a first visit. Eight works if you keep to one half of the island, and fourteen lets you add the east coast or a second park without rushing.

homeQuestions.q: Do we have our own driver?
homeQuestions.a: Yes. Every journey comes with a private vehicle and a driver who stays with you from the airport to the airport. They know the roads, the stops and the good lunch places, and they are happy to change the plan on the day.

homeQuestions.q: Can we make the trip work for children?
homeQuestions.a: Yes. Shorter drives, rooms with space to spread out, and an elephant morning that is worth the early start. Sri Lanka With Little Ones shows how we shape it.

homeQuestions.q: What is included in a proposed trip?
homeQuestions.a: Stays, the vehicle and driver, transfers, and the park entries and activities listed in the plan. Flights, meals beyond breakfast, and tips are not, and we say so line by line.

homeQuestions.q: Can the route change while we travel?
homeQuestions.a: Within reason, yes. We build slack into every plan so a place that holds you longer than expected does not break the week.

homeQuestions.q: How do we choose the right coast?
homeQuestions.a: By the month you travel. The south and west are dry from December to April, the east from May to September. Our month by month guide covers it, and we will talk it through.
